source.inspection: Re-extracted and reread complete one-based PDF pages 28-30, 55, and 60-62 for this v2 review. checked_source_evidence.evidence: The chapter-1 PI uses reversible-semigroup Dirichlet energy and a broad L2(pi) formulation. It is not identical to a theorem restricted to compact Euclidean tests. The sketch does not supply the complete form-domain/core closure argument.
The Langevin PI has coefficient C_PI in Var_pi(f) <= C_PI integral ||grad f||^2 d pi. KL(mu||pi) is defined using the actual Radon-Nikodym density, not merely a compensated real-valued integral.

Density LSI is KL(rho*pi||pi) <= (C_LSI/2) E(rho,log rho). The text gives C_PI <= C_LSI via positive small-epsilon linearization. In the Euclidean specialization the energy equals FI, which equals 4 integral ||grad sqrt(rho)||^2 d pi; function-form LSI consequently has coefficient 2*C_LSI.

The exercise requests linearization of LSI to PI. Its hint uses smooth compactly supported centered f and the quadratic KL coefficient (1/2) integral f^2 d pi. The scalar calculus, domination, admissibility, energy limit, and extensions are omitted analytical work.

Both Euclidean PI and function-form LSI are explicitly stated on every C_c^infinity(R^d) test. PI does not impose centering. The coefficients are respectively C_PI and 2*C_LSI. This exactly supports the selected compact Euclidean subtarget and starting assumption.

checked_source_evidence.anchor: Approximation paragraph, inequality relationships, and Proposition 2.1.1
checked_source_evidence.evidence: Wider test-class extension is attributed to density arguments with a pointer to Bakry et al. (2014, Chapter 3), not proved here. The direct Exercise 1.7 route is distinguished from the route through T2. Proposition 2.1.1 permits bounded smooth centered f whose gradient has compact support; f need not be compactly supported.

The proof takes f satisfying the preceding proposition and explicitly applies (1.E.1) at its KL comparison. It is therefore a genuine consumer of the bounded-centered expansion on the compact-gradient class. Its T2 and transport-linearization ingredients are not prerequisites of the direct Exercise 1.7 route.

verdict_summary: The exact v2 proposal correctly selects the compact Euclidean PI subtarget, preserves the open whole-exercise/form-domain/abstract boundaries, orders centered-test PI before uncentering, explicitly retains the compact-LSI extension gap, uses the source constants, and records the broader real downstream KL consumer. The finite-measure compensated-integral packet remains a useful strictly smaller prerequisite. No further required topology repair was found within this expressly bounded scope.

selected_subtarget.finding: Starting with Ent_pi(u^2) <= 2*C integral ||grad u||^2 for every compact smooth u and targeting Var_pi(g) <= C integral ||grad g||^2 for every compact smooth g matches PDF60. One finite positive C is fixed independently of tests and epsilon. The use of a probability measure and Euclidean gradient energy does not itself assert that every such measure has a Langevin semigroup.

whole_exercise_boundary.finding: The compact target is explicitly not equated with the broad chapter-1 L2/form-domain or abstract reversible-semigroup statement. The whole-exercise-boundary node is an unresolved boundary marker, not a proved target or an outgoing theorem implication. An abstract-energy route and a Euclidean core/closure extension are different residual tasks; neither is certified here.

centering_order.finding: For g compact smooth, f=g-integral g d pi is bounded, smooth, centered, and has compactly supported gradient, but usually lacks compact support. V2 records this accurately. The centered-test-pi -> poincare-test-extension edge supplies the restricted-PI premise before uncentering; the centered-bounded-test edge separately supplies the chosen f and its unchanged gradient. The final g is not required to be centered.

compact_lsi_extension.finding: The actual square-root density is generally noncompact, so it cannot be admitted to compact-test LSI merely by positivity. V2 keeps a separate cutoff/limit/admissibility node before actual-lsi-application. That is the right topology and does not pretend that the missing analytical proof is present.
proof_obligations_already_inside_this_no: Construct admissible compact smooth approximants to sqrt(1+epsilon*f).
Prove convergence of entropy, including both the integral of z log z and the normalization term, with the usual continuous value at z=0.
Control cutoff-gradient terms and establish convergence of the actual square-gradient energy.
Relate the normalized entropy to canonical probability KL only after mass one and density identification.

constants.finding: The function-form coefficient 2*C becomes C/2 times FI because FI=4 integral ||grad sqrt(rho)||^2. With rho=1+epsilon*f, FI/epsilon^2 equals integral ||grad f||^2/(1+epsilon*f) d pi. The KL/epsilon^2 limit is (1/2) integral f^2 d pi. Hence the limiting inequality is integral f^2 <= C integral ||grad f||^2, with the same admissible C. This yields C_PI <= C_LSI for optimal constants, not equality of optimal constants.

corollary_consumer.finding: The probability-kl-expansion -> corollary-2-1-2 edge has the correct direction and explicit use site at PDF62. Its bounded smooth centered compact-gradient class is the one stated on PDF61, not the narrower compact-support hint. The consumer is marked observed and outside this packet's proof scope; no transport theorem or T2 hypothesis was added to the direct LSI route.

graph_assessment.coverage: The two textual regions of Exercise 1.7 are represented. V2 additionally inventories the normalizations/test-class conventions and the actual broader consumer. Neighboring exercises and the rest of the chapter are not claimed covered. The source supplies no additional worked proof paragraph inside Exercise 1.7.
graph_assessment.source_gap_provenance: The scalar/DCT, probability, cutoff, energy and centering nodes are rigorous analytical obligations reconstructed to fill omissions. Their SOURCE_GAP labels correctly avoid attributing completed proofs to the source or to the implementation.
graph_assessment.directions: The scalar coefficient feeds the dominated integral, which feeds the probability expansion. Normalization/positivity feeds both the probability and energy routes. The actual finite-epsilon LSI application and its two limiting coefficients feed centered-test PI, which feeds uncentering and then the compact target. No reversal was found.
graph_assessment.conditional_discharge: V2 makes the needed conditional premises visible as nodes and dependency edges. They are scheduled to be discharged, not declared discharged by this review. In particular the extension theorem and genuine finite-epsilon energy remain proof obligations.
graph_assessment.false_ands: No false AND was found in the selected direct route. Corollary 2.1.2 and the LSI -> T2 -> PI alternative are downstream/alternative source material, not conjunctive prerequisites of the compact direct route.
graph_assessment.background_detail: The review explicitly checked the canonical KL definition at PDF29 as well as the v2 standing-conventions anchors. A later full source inventory can split the combined standing-conventions record into individual definition/use-site records; this is not a missing mathematical bridge in the bounded v2 plan.

first_packet_assessment.exact_boundary: For finite mu and a.e.-strongly-measurable real f with a finite essential bound, establish the punctured epsilon-to-zero limit of integral q(1+epsilon*f)/epsilon^2 d mu to (1/2) integral f^2 d mu, where q(u)=u log u-u+1 and the logarithm is used in its eventual positive region.
first_packet_assessment.why_useful: It is the genuine dominated second-order integral step behind the hint and the bounded-centered KL expansion. Its bounded-function generality supports both centering arbitrary compact PI tests and the compact-gradient class consumed in Corollary 2.1.2.
not_required_for_this_leaf: Log-concavity, strong convexity, or finite second moments
Canonical KL, Fisher, LSI, PI, or transport conclusions
essential_contracts: The scalar coefficient is proved by genuine calculus, including q(1)=q'(1)=0.
The eventual positive lower bound and the M=0 case are handled without division by zero.
An actual integrable quadratic envelope and measurable integrands justify passing the limit through the integral.
A value assigned to a totalized quotient at epsilon=0 is not a proof of the punctured limit.
